traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Labiatae (read 2026-10-17): lamina entire or dissected, dissected ones pinnatifid or palmatifid; Flora of China family page (read 2026-10-17): simple to pinnately divided. Most species have undivided blades.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Lucid family key, Lamiaceae (read 2026-10-17): leaves usually toothed; margins entire, crenate, dentate, serrate or sinuate. Reed College family page (read 2026-10-17): margin often serrate. DELTA, Labiatae (read 2026-10-17): entire, crenate or serrate. Wikipedia Salvia (read 2026-10-17): often entire, sometimes toothed, which keeps entire in the list.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Lucid family key, Lamiaceae (read 2026-10-17): blade outlines linear, lanceolate, ovate, elliptic, oblong, oblanceolate, orbicular and needle-like; bases may be cordate. Ranking ours, weighted by genus size (Wikipedia Lamiaceae (read 2026-10-17) gives Salvia c. 900, Scutellaria 360, Stachys 300, Plectranthus 300, Hyptis 280 species): these mostly have ovate blades; narrow blades in Thymus and many shrubby Mediterranean genera.

traits.perianth.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 416: perianth biseriate, a 5-lobed fused calyx and a fused 4- or 5-lobed corolla (formula K (5) C (5)).

traits.carpels.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 416: gynoecium of 2 carpels, divided by false septa into 4 locules (formula G (2)).

traits.ovary_position.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 416: flowers hypogynous, ovary superior and often deeply 4-lobed with a gynobasic style.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 416: Simpson states the hypanthium is absent and the flowers hypogynous.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 342 Labiatae: herbs, rarely woody, often scented, the stems usually square; leaves opposite or whorled, simple; no stipules; flowers irregular, rarely almost regular; calyx of 5 joined sepals, often two-lipped; corolla a tube of 4 or 5 lobes, often two-lipped; stamens 4 or 2 on the tube; ovary superior, two carpels deeply lobed with the style from between the lobes; fruit 4 nutlets, read here as a schizocarp of four mericarps. APG's Lamiaceae also takes in woody genera Hutchinson kept in Verbenaceae (family 243: Vitex, Callicarpa, teak), with drupes and some palmately compound leaves: so woody is stated as sometimes, compound leaves as rare and the drupe as sometimes (inferred, not traced). The order (Lamiales) states the stipules, the ovary and the two carpels.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Labiatae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded no rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.life_span.note: Britannica, Lamiaceae (read 2026-10-16): most members are perennial or annual herbs and some are woody shrubs or subshrubs; the woody members are all perennial, so perennial leads; no page read mentions biennials, so that state is dropped rather than kept as rarely.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Labiatae: flowers regular or irregular as coded, a state the authors qualify keeping its word (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); the corolla rarely almost regular (Mentha), so actinomorphic is rare.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Labiatae: its irregular flowers have a two-lipped corolla, read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy bilabiate.

traits.stipules.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 416, 417, 418, family Lamiaceae: stipules false; read as false.

traits.inflorescence.note: DELTA Labiatae (read 2026-10-17): flowers usually in verticils built from axillary pairs of cymes, the ultimate units cymose; solitary flowers also listed. Weighted by Wikipedia Lamiaceae genus sizes: whorl-of-cymes genera Salvia (~900), Stachys (~300), Plectranthus (~300), Hyptis (~280), Teucrium (~250), Vitex (~250), Thymus (~220), Nepeta (~200) far outnumber Scutellaria (~360), whose flowers sit singly or paired in the axils. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.fruit_type.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add berry (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 416, 417, 418: schizocarp of usually 4 (1-3) nutlets, or drupe or berry.

traits.stem_cross_section.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 416, 417, 418, family Lamiaceae: stems four-sided (square), at least when young; Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) agrees (square); read as {"square": "usually"}.
